about: A full intake call for Denver Lang, the sample patient, following the call plan: goal first, then conditions, medicines, care team, what has helped and reminders. Each turn has both sides and the notepad after it. The simulated call test speaks Denver's lines and checks the transcript, the notes and the proposed notebooks against this script.

turns.agent: Hi, I'm Stellis. In the next five minutes I'll learn what you want help with, your conditions, medicines and care team, and what reminders would help. I'll take notes as we go, and you can edit them. First, what's the main health goal you'd like help with?
turns.person: Keeping the weight off. I've lost about eight kilos since April last year, and I'd like my knees to stop hurting on the stairs.

notes.heading: Goals
items: Keep the weight off, after losing about 8 kg since April 2024

turns.agent: Eight kilos is real progress. Which knee is it, and how bad is the pain on the stairs now?
turns.person: The right one. Physio got it from a six to about a three out of ten.

notes.heading: Goals
items: Keep the weight off, after losing about 8 kg since April 2024
Less pain in the right knee on stairs, now about 3 out of 10, down from 6

turns.agent: That's a big drop. Next, your conditions. Do you have any ongoing conditions I should know about?
turns.person: Type two diabetes and high blood pressure, since the eighties. And I had bypass surgery in ninety seven.

notes.heading: Goals
items: Keep the weight off, after losing about 8 kg since April 2024
Less pain in the right knee on stairs, now about 3 out of 10, down from 6

turns.agent: Thank you. What medicines do you take, with the dose and time of day?
turns.person: Metformin five hundred in the morning, lisinopril, and simvastatin at night.

notes.heading: Goals

Less pain in the right knee on stairs, now about 3 out of 10, down from 6

turns.agent: Did you say lisinopril, the blood pressure medicine?
turns.person: Yes, lisinopril. They stopped my water pill last year because I got dizzy standing up.

turns.person: My family doctor, Doctor Patel, a dietitian, and a personal trainer.

turns.agent: What has helped most with your weight and your knee so far?

turns.agent: Here is what I heard. You want to keep the weight off and ease your right knee on the stairs. You manage diabetes and blood pressure with metformin, lisinopril and simvastatin. You see Dr. Patel, a dietitian, a physiotherapist and a trainer, and you'd like a Monday weigh-in reminder. I'll suggest notebooks for weight and knees, and for diabetes and heart care. Is anything wrong?
Thank you, Denver. Your notes are ready to review. [END]
